title: Complex number
summary: Complex numbers can be constructed as ordered pairs of reals with explicit field operations.

context.framework: ordered-pair construction over the real field
context.note: Revision 2 supplies equality, addition, multiplication, zero, one, and i rather than only multiplication.

assumptions.text: The complete ordered field of real numbers is fixed.

content.plain: Represent a complex number by a pair of real coordinates and define arithmetic so that the second coordinate behaves like a square root of minus one.
content.exact: Let C=R×R with componentwise equality, (a,b)+(c,d)=(a+c,b+d), and (a,b)·(c,d)=(ac−bd,ad+bc). Define 0_C=(0,0), 1_C=(1,0), and i=(0,1). Then i²=(-1,0), identified with the embedded real number -1.
content.caveat: The displayed operations define the construction; the field laws and uniqueness up to suitable isomorphism are separate theorems.

verification.method: QEVA 0.5 protocol audit corrected scope, assumptions, and dependency semantics; no formal proof is claimed.

provenance.creator: QEVA 0.5 mathematical protocol audit
provenance.source_note: Completes the pair construction enough to identify the operations and distinguished elements. This is an original QEVA formulation and remains subject to independent review.
